evals.prompt: Where should I add a new REST endpoint for product reviews? Walk me through which files to touch.
evals.expected_output: Concrete list of backend files/packages to create or modify: new model, repository, service, controller, DTOs and mapper. Should mention the correct base package (msg.onlineshopapi), follow the existing layered pattern, and optionally note where a frontend feature folder would go.
expectations: Lists all required backend layers: model/entity, repository, service, controller, DTO, and mapper
References the correct base package (msg.onlineshopapi) or the correct directory structure
Mentions that a Flyway migration file is needed for the schema change
Correctly locates DTOs in dto/ and mapper in dto/mapper/
Mentions frontend impact: at minimum an Angular service method, ideally also a MSW mock handler

evals.prompt: How does auth work end-to-end in this app?
evals.expected_output: End-to-end explanation covering: login POST /auth/login → JwtService generates token → stored in localStorage → AuthTokenInterceptor attaches Bearer header → JwtAuthFilter validates on backend → SecurityContext populated. Should mention roles (CUSTOMER/ADMIN), @PreAuthorize, and the Angular guards (authGuard, rolesGuard).
expectations: Mentions JWT token generation (JwtService or equivalent)
Mentions localStorage as where the token is stored on the frontend
Mentions AuthTokenInterceptor as the mechanism that attaches the Bearer header
Mentions JwtAuthFilter as the backend token validation component
Mentions user roles (ADMIN and CUSTOMER) and @PreAuthorize for method-level enforcement
Mentions Angular guards (authGuard and/or rolesGuard) for route protection

evals.prompt: What pattern does the app use to pick which warehouse fulfills an order, and where is it configured?
evals.expected_output: Identifies the Strategy pattern, names both implementations (SingleLocationStrategy, MostAbundantStrategy), explains what each does, and points to app.order.strategy in application.yml as the config key.
expectations: Correctly identifies the Strategy design pattern
Names at least one concrete strategy implementation class
Names both strategy implementations (SingleLocation and MostAbundant/MultipleLocations variants)
Points to application.yml or application-local.yml as the configuration location (mentioning app.order.strategy key is a bonus)
Explains the behavioral difference between the two strategies
